<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command sources the PKGBUILD in a restricted context, executing only top-level code and not running any of the package functions (`pkgver`, `prepare`, `build`, `package`, etc.). In this PKGBUILD, the top-level content consists solely of variable assignments and a `case` statement that sets an architecture mapping based on the value of `CARCH`. All variables are defined using static or templated strings derived from package metadata, with no command substitution, external downloads, or execution of remote code.

There are no function calls, loops, or conditional executions at the top level that could trigger side effects. The use of parameterized URLs and architecture mappings is standard in AUR packages and does not introduce risk during the `--printsrcinfo` phase, as no sources are downloaded or verified at this stage. The checksums are present and pinned, though even if they were `SKIP`, that would not affect the safety of this operation.

Thus, sourcing this PKGBUILD for metadata extraction poses no security risk.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>No dangerous top-level code in PKGBUILD</summary>
